title: Recorded time and barycentric terms cannot explain the selected 2021 GJ 191 velocity difference under stated bounds
abstract: We test three timing mechanisms for a known difference between DRS and SERVAL velocities of GJ 191. We use 32 public HARPS-RVBank version 02 exposures in eight nights from 2021. Separate night offsets and slopes leave 3.198 m/s RMS. The stored barycentric correction difference leaves only 0.00657 m/s RMS after the same projection. Bounds for the listed time difference, midpoint versus photon-mean timing, and finite exposure effects are too small to explain the full residual. Even their conservative sum can reach at most 37.45 percent of the weighted residual norm. This is a deterministic mechanism test under accurate metadata, bounded Earth acceleration and curvature, and a scalar velocity approximation. It does not require a Gaussian error law. Incorrect metadata, wavelength-dependent exposure weights, and other reduction errors remain open. All products share spectra. No planet, physical cause, or independent confirmation is found. Code, bounds, source hashes, an original figure, and external retrieval steps are included. External records remain outside the bundle.

display.caption: Conservative upper bounds on the weighted residual norm explained by each stated mechanism. The sum allows arbitrary signs and includes duplicate allowances. It still falls below the observed norm.
